page: Amazon Web Services m8a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the platform features 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The system includes 768.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no local storage drives and zero GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data positions the m8a.metal-48xl in the top tier across several computing profiles. In synthetic stress tests, stress-ng multi-core reached 706,732.18 and PassMark CPU score measured 185,003.99. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrated 1,037.85 GB/sec for read operations and 456.39 GB/sec for write operations. Application performance is highlighted by 458.91 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 179.54 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based inference workloads recorded 5,422.95 tokens per second for small 135M parameter models and 581.4 tokens per second for medium 7B models during prompt processing.

The bare-metal setup eliminates hypervisor virtualization overhead, optimizing resource efficiency for compute density and direct hardware access. A primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of bundled local storage, requiring workloads to utilize networked storage volumes over the 75 Gbps interface. The server profile is suited for massive container orchestration platforms, in-memory databases, large-scale software compilation, batch processing pipelines, and high-concurrency web tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor platform. It provides 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs with a single thread per core, running at up to 4.5 GHz. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation. The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage and no dedicated graphics accelerators, backed by a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark assessments place the system in the top tier for multi-core computation, raw memory bandwidth, and high-throughput Redis caching operations. Due to its bare-metal architecture and high core count, the m8a.metal-48xl is structured for multi-threaded compilation, high-traffic web infrastructure, memory-intensive data analytics, and enterprise container environments that leverage networked storage volumes.
